source: This app's own 8-layer prompt system (tools/prompt_bank.json + tools/realism_lint.py), plus slot structure reverse-engineered from worked prompts - the `beauty-macro` and `macro-insert` templates from a community-supplied macro/beauty-portrait prompt contributed by the user (the same prompt tools/macro_insert_bank.json harvests its vocabulary from), and `photoreal-portrait` from this app's own build_prompt.py compose order. The `video-sequence` template is reverse-engineered from a community-supplied luxury-vlog video prompt contributed by the user, and `video-shot` from this app's own tools/motion_lint.py rules (which DO transcribe the bootcamp's Kling camera-movement toolkit, via tools/motion_bank.json). The `action-commercial` template is reverse-engineered from a second, different community-supplied video prompt contributed by the user (a high-action car commercial) - see its own `source_note` for how its shape differs from video-sequence. The `product-campaign` template is reverse-engineered from a THIRD community-supplied prompt contributed by the user (a confectionery campaign portrait), and is the image-side sibling of `action-commercial`: the same banded-brief house style, but one still frame with a person and a package in it. Everything else here is NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material.
note: A template is an ORDERED list of slots - the skeleton of a prompt, not its words. This bank teaches structure; the vocabulary banks (prompt_bank, lighting_bank, style_bank, macro_insert_bank, ...) supply what goes in each slot. Every template also declares `kind` - 'image' or 'video' - so the Anatomy tab's picker can group them instead of listing all five as one undifferentiated list; a template produces exactly one kind of prompt, never both, so this is a fixed fact about the template rather than a per-run choice. Detection is deliberately split: a slot that maps onto one of the eight gated realism layers declares `layer` and is detected by tools/realism_lint.py's OWN DETECT table - never a second copy of those keywords, the same no-duplication rule tools/relight_bank.json follows for lighting and camera-angle phrases. Only slots the eight layers do not cover carry their own `detect` list - and a slot whose vocabulary already lives in ANOTHER linter borrows it by name instead: a `borrow` of 'motion-verbs' takes tools/motion_lint.py's own MOTION_VERBS, so the camera-movement slots cannot drift away from what that linter actually gates on. The video templates also record two facts about this app that a prompt written elsewhere will trip over: tools/sound_bank.json is effects-only and its linter rejects music vocabulary outright (hence a separate `music` slot), and tools/build_story.py distinguishes clip_seconds from edit_seconds (hence the shot-sequence slot's warning that two-second beats are edit lengths, not generation lengths). `analyse()` is keyword presence, not parsing: it answers 'which slots does this prompt appear to fill', which is honest, rather than pretending to segment free prose into semantic regions.

beauty-macro.label: Beauty macro portrait
beauty-macro.summary: An extreme close-up beauty portrait where the skin itself is the subject. Fifteen slots; slots 7-10 are the ones that separate real skin from plastic skin.
beauty-macro.source_note: Reverse-engineered from the community-supplied FULL FACE prompt.

slots.label: Framing + subject
slots.does: States the shot type and who is in it, in one breath.
slots.why: The model needs the frame before the detail. 'Extreme close-up beauty portrait of X' front-loads both.
slots.example: extreme close-up, straight-on beauty portrait of a blonde woman with blue eyes, looking directly into the camera

slots.label: Styling
slots.does: Hair and wardrobe, described as they affect the frame.
slots.why: In a beauty macro, hair is mostly a negative space decision - slicking it back is what exposes the face.
slots.example: hair slicked straight back in a wet-look style, exposing the entire face, temples and hairline

slots.label: Composition
slots.does: Where the subject sits in the frame and where the camera is relative to it.
slots.why: Symmetry and camera height are decisions, not defaults. Saying nothing gets you the model's average.
slots.example: symmetrical front-facing composition, camera perfectly level with her eyes, face centred in frame

slots.label: Expression
slots.does: The face's state - mouth, eyes, tension.
slots.why: Unstated, models drift to a slight smile. 'Neutral, lips gently closed' is a real instruction.
slots.example: neutral relaxed expression, lips gently closed

slots.label: Camera
slots.does: Names an actual capture device.
slots.why: This is the single highest-value realism word. A named camera implies a whole optical rendering.
slots.example: captured on a full-frame high-resolution camera

slots.label: Lens and focus
slots.does: Focal length, aperture, and what is sharp.
slots.why: 100mm macro is what makes pore detail physically plausible rather than hallucinated.
slots.example: 100mm macro portrait lens, extremely sharp focus across the eyes and central features

slots.label: Skin: surface
slots.does: The literal surface - pores, lines, blemishes.
slots.why: Slot one of four. On its own this still reads retouched; it needs the next three.
slots.example: visible pores across the forehead, nose and cheeks, microscopic fine lines, faint blemishes

slots.label: Skin: variation
slots.does: States that skin tone is NOT uniform across the face.
slots.why: The most-skipped slot, and the biggest single tell. Real faces are redder at the nose and cooler at the forehead; a uniform tone is the plastic look.
slots.example: natural tonal variation between forehead, cheeks, nose and chin - never a single uniform skin tone

slots.label: Skin: light behaviour
slots.does: How light enters and leaves the skin - peach fuzz catching it, blood tones beneath it.
slots.why: Skin is translucent. Prompts that treat it as an opaque surface get waxwork results no amount of 'detailed' fixes.
slots.example: fine translucent peach fuzz catching the light along the jawline, subsurface scattering warming the thinnest skin

slots.label: Individual features
slots.does: Brows, lashes, irises - resolved as individual fibres, with asymmetry stated.
slots.why: 'Perfect' features read as CGI. Naming irregular density and slight asymmetry is what buys realism.
slots.example: individual eyebrow hairs with irregular density, individual eyelashes without perfect uniformity, slight natural asymmetry

slots.label: Hair detail
slots.does: Strand separation, baby hairs, moisture.
slots.why: Hair rendered as a mass is a giveaway; rendered as separable sections it is not.
slots.example: separated into realistic individual strands and small damp sections, fine baby hairs at the hairline

slots.label: Lighting
slots.does: Source, direction, size, and the shadows it makes.
slots.why: 'Soft light' is not a lighting instruction. Direction plus source size is.
slots.example: soft directional beauty lighting from slightly above and camera-left, a large diffused source casting delicate dimensional shadows, realistic shadows with gentle falloff toward the jaw

slots.label: Background
slots.does: What is behind the subject, and that it does not compete.
slots.why: Unstated, the model invents one - usually a busy one.
slots.example: neutral light grey studio background with no distractions

slots.label: Negatives
slots.does: Names the retouching operations you do not want.
slots.why: The key principle: name the PROCESS, not the look. 'No frequency separation, no pore removal' is far more precise than 'not fake'.
slots.example: no beauty filter, no skin smoothing, no frequency separation, no pore removal, no facial reshaping

slots.label: Aesthetic framing
slots.does: One closing line naming the genre the image belongs to.
slots.why: Anchors everything above to a real-world reference the model has seen thousands of.
slots.example: raw high-end editorial beauty photography, intimate skincare-campaign aesthetic

macro-insert.label: Macro insert (feature crop)
macro-insert.summary: The short, repeatable template for an extreme macro of ONE feature of a face that already exists. Five slots - and the last one is the whole trick.
macro-insert.source_note: Reverse-engineered from the community-supplied EYE / MOUTH / CHEEK prompts. Implemented by tools/build_macro_insert.py.

slots.label: Render instruction
slots.does: States that this is a macro render of a region.
slots.why: Sets scale before anything else, so the detail list below is read at the right magnification.
slots.example: render an extreme ultra-realistic macro of the eye

slots.label: Region
slots.does: Which feature fills the frame, and what is cropped away.
slots.why: Saying what is NOT in frame is what stops the model pulling back to a portrait.
slots.example: extreme close-up, one eye filling the entire frame, brow and cheekbone cropped away

slots.label: Region detail list
slots.does: The anatomy specific to this region only.
slots.why: Each region has its own vocabulary - iris fibres and sclera vessels for an eye, vermilion border and philtrum for a mouth. Generic 'detailed' does nothing here.
slots.example: detailed iris fibres, dark limbal ring, individual eyelashes and roots, wet tear-film reflections, fine sclera vessels, natural eyelid texture

slots.label: No-retouch clause
slots.does: One short negative, scoped to this crop.
slots.why: At macro scale smoothing is instantly visible, so this is worth repeating per insert rather than relying on the base prompt.
slots.example: no smoothing or retouching

slots.label: Preserve clause
slots.does: Names exactly which properties of the reference must not change.
slots.why: THE load-bearing slot. Without it a macro crop becomes a different person's eye. A general identity lock never says 'gaze', 'lip proportions' or 'undertone' - this does.
slots.example: preserve the exact eye colour, shape, eyelid position, gaze and identity

photoreal-portrait.label: Photoreal portrait (this app's own default)
photoreal-portrait.summary: Eight slots - the eight-layer skeleton tools/build_prompt.py composes by default, in its own order. Shown here so you can compare it against the macro templates above and see exactly what they add.
photoreal-portrait.source_note: This app's own build_prompt.py LAYER_ORDER and tools/prompt_bank.json.

slots.label: Core realism triggers
slots.does: Three words or phrases asserting photorealism up front.
slots.why: Cheap and load-bearing; the rest of the prompt is read in this frame.
slots.example: ultra-realistic, photorealistic, true-to-life textures

slots.label: Camera
slots.does: Names a capture device.
slots.why: Implies a whole optical rendering in two words.
slots.example: DSLR photography

slots.label: Lens
slots.does: Focal length and depth of field.
slots.why: Controls how much of the frame is sharp, which reads as physical rather than generated.
slots.example: shot on an 85mm portrait lens, shallow depth of field

slots.label: Lighting
slots.does: Source, direction, quality.
slots.why: See tools/lighting_bank.json for the full vocabulary - this is the deepest toolkit in the app.
slots.example: soft natural daylight with realistic shadows

slots.label: Texture
slots.does: Surface detail and imperfection.
slots.why: The layer the macro templates above explode into four separate slots.
slots.example: visible skin pores, slight imperfections

slots.label: Colour
slots.does: Grade and restraint.
slots.why: Stated restraint prevents the oversaturated AI look.
slots.example: natural colour grading, realistic contrast

slots.label: Composition
slots.does: Framing and subject separation.
slots.why: See tools/composition_bank.json and tools/camera_angle_bank.json.
slots.example: eye-level shot, foreground and background separation

slots.label: Grain and capture quality
slots.does: Sensor noise, dynamic range, the absence of over-polish.
slots.why: The final anti-CGI signal.
slots.example: subtle film grain, sharp focus, not overly polished

video-sequence.label: Timed video sequence (locks + shots)
video-sequence.summary: A whole short video in one prompt: three locks that must not drift, one pass of global look and sound, then a timed shot list with its own dialogue. Thirteen slots, and the first three are the ones that decide whether it is still the same video by the end.
video-sequence.source_note: Reverse-engineered from a community-supplied luxury-vlog video prompt contributed by the user. NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material.

slots.label: Character lock
slots.does: Describes the person once, in terms that stay true from the first frame to the last.
slots.why: Lock one of three. A video model re-decides the face at every cut unless you state it is the same person - tools/motion_bank.json's avatar_guard exists for the same reason and its first line is literally 'no identity drift between cuts'. Describe build and bearing, never a passing pose: anything that changes shot to shot does not belong in a lock.
slots.example: CHARACTER LOCK: tall slim athletic woman, elegant natural beauty, effortless confidence, consistent identity in every shot

slots.label: Outfit lock
slots.does: Pins the wardrobe - garment, cut, fabric and colour - as a separate statement from the person.
slots.why: Lock two of three, and the one most often folded into the character lock by mistake. An identity lock says nothing about clothes, so the model is free to re-dress her between cuts; naming the cut and the fabric is what survives a change of angle. This app has no outfit-lock tool - build_prompt.py locks identity, build_relight.py locks scene - so this slot is written out by hand.
slots.example: OUTFIT LOCK: powder-blue premium activewear set - ruched sports bra, sculpting high-waisted leggings, luxe fitted fabric, unchanged throughout

slots.label: Environment lock
slots.does: Fixes the room: its size, its materials, its furniture, its light sources.
slots.why: Lock three of three. Cutting between a wide and a close-up is where invented architecture appears - a different floor, a ceiling twice as high. State the ceiling height and the floor material explicitly; they are the two a model reinvents first.
slots.example: ENVIRONMENT LOCK: upscale boutique wellness studio, realistic domestic ceiling height, warm cream walls, oak floors, designer mirrors, candles and plants, one aerial silk rig

slots.label: Style
slots.does: One line naming the genre and the capture register the whole video sits in.
slots.why: It applies to every shot at once, so it is stated once at the top rather than repeated per beat. This is where a hybrid belongs - 'iPhone realism with a cinematic grade' is a real instruction; 'cinematic' on its own is not.
slots.example: STYLE: luxury lifestyle vlog, clean expensive taste, realistic iPhone capture with a cinematic grade, no CGI look

slots.label: Lighting
slots.does: The light the whole piece is shot in - source, direction, warmth.
slots.why: A global lighting line is also a continuity lock: without one, each shot invents its own time of day. See tools/lighting_bank.json for the vocabulary.
slots.example: LIGHTING: warm golden interior glow, soft window light from camera-left, flattering natural skin tones

slots.label: Music bed
slots.does: The scored track under the whole video - genre, tempo, and how loud it sits.
slots.why: Deliberately its own slot, because this app's tools/sound_bank.json is effects-ONLY: sound_lint rejects every word in that bank's own not_effects list - music, song, melody, soundtrack, background score, singing, lyrics, instrumental and the narration words - so a music bed can never come from that bank. Note what is NOT on that list: 'beat' and 'hip-hop' pass the music gate, and a line like 'chic upbeat lounge hip-hop beat' fails a different check instead, for naming an object rather than a sound. The bed belongs here in the video prompt, or in your editor - never in a sound-effects brief.
slots.example: MUSIC: chic upbeat lounge hip-hop, subtle bass, sitting low under the dialogue

slots.label: Diegetic sound
slots.does: The sounds the scene itself makes - room tone, footsteps, handled objects.
slots.why: The half tools/sound_bank.json genuinely covers, in its own three layers: ambience, key sound, accent. Naming what the body and the props do is what stops a video reading as a silent clip with music pasted over it.
slots.example: SOUND: quiet room tone, footsteps on oak floor, fabric movement, a water bottle set down on wood

slots.label: Voice
slots.does: How the spoken lines sound - register, pace, distance from the mic.
slots.why: Separate from what is said. See tools/voice_bank.json's sixteen styles; a tone named once at the top keeps every line in the shot list consistent.
slots.example: VOICE: soft feminine vlog tone, calm and playful, close-mic and conversational

slots.label: On-screen text
slots.does: States what appears as graphics - or explicitly that nothing does.
slots.why: 'None' is a real answer and worth writing down. Video models volunteer garbled captions and watermarks unprompted, so an explicit 'no on-screen text' is a working instruction, not a blank line.
slots.example: TEXT: none - no captions, no subtitles, no lower thirds

slots.label: Camera behaviour
slots.does: How the camera moves, and how the piece is cut.
slots.why: Movement first: tools/motion_lint.py's rule one is that a video prompt leads with the camera, because that is what the model latches onto. One dominant move per shot - pushing in and pulling out at once is the classic failure the same linter catches.
slots.example: CAMERA: smooth handheld vlog cuts, the camera drifts in for intimate close-ups, polished handheld rather than gimbal-smooth

slots.label: Shot sequence
slots.does: The timed beat list - a timestamp, a name, and what is in frame.
slots.why: The structural slot. Mind the distinction tools/build_story.py already draws between clip_seconds (what the model generates, and most will not go below about five) and edit_seconds (what survives your cut): seven beats across fifteen seconds averages barely two seconds each, so those are edit lengths. Generate each beat long, then trim it short.
slots.example: [00:00-00:02 | Intro arrival] front-facing selfie entering the studio, sunglasses pushed up, tote bag on the shoulder

slots.label: Dialogue
slots.does: The actual words, attached to the beat that carries them.
slots.why: Written per beat rather than as one block, and kept short - a line has to fit the seconds you gave it. Mark which lines are on camera and which are voice-over: the model lip-syncs the first and not the second.
slots.example: Dialogue: 'Come to class with me - I needed a reset today.' Dialogue (VO): 'This studio is honestly a dream.'

slots.label: Negative prompt
slots.does: Names the video-specific failures you do not want.
slots.why: Video has failure modes stills do not: jitter, flicker, drifting identity, bad lip sync, limbs clipping through props. tools/motion_bank.json already carries a negatives list and an opt-in avatar_guard - start from those rather than inventing a list.
slots.example: NEGATIVE PROMPT: no warped limbs, no stiff robotic movement, no bad lip sync, no jitter or flicker between cuts, no plastic skin, no clipping through props

video-shot.label: Single video shot (this app's own gate)
video-shot.summary: Six slots - the shape tools/motion_lint.py actually scores one shot against. Use it per beat of the sequence template above, or on its own for a single clip.
video-shot.source_note: This app's own motion_lint.py rules and tools/motion_bank.json, which transcribe the AI Video Bootcamp Kling camera-movement toolkit.

slots.label: Camera lead
slots.does: Opens the prompt with the camera move, before anything else.
slots.why: Rule one, in the toolkit's own words: 'always start your prompt with the camera angle, this way Kling recognizes it immediately'. motion_lint.py checks only the first ninety characters for it.
slots.example: the camera slowly pushes in toward her

slots.label: Subject
slots.does: Who or what the move is aimed at.
slots.why: Rule two: 'if you say tracking over the shoulder but there is no character in your scene, Kling will get confused'. The move and the subject have to agree.
slots.example: a woman in her powder-blue activewear

slots.label: Action
slots.does: One thing the subject does, in the present tense.
slots.why: Rule six: one action, not a chain. 'Walking while talking while eating' confuses a video model exactly the way two competing camera moves do.
slots.example: reaches up and grips the silk

slots.label: Setting
slots.does: Where it happens, in enough detail to be lit.
slots.why: Rule five catches contradictions between the move and the place - a camera that dives underwater in a kitchen. The setting is what makes that checkable.
slots.example: in a warm boutique studio with oak floors

slots.label: Capture style
slots.does: The camera and grade, as one closing phrase.
slots.why: tools/motion_bank.json ships ready-made style_presets for exactly this slot - pick one rather than writing your own.
slots.example: shot on an iPhone, raw handheld look, natural colour grading

slots.label: Negative guard
slots.does: The trailing no-warp, no-morph guard.
slots.why: Rule seven. compose() appends it automatically, so this slot is really a check that a hand-edited prompt has not lost it.
slots.example: no warped face, no floating limbs, no distorted hands, no morphing

action-commercial.label: High-action commercial (render/look/grade + timed shots)
action-commercial.summary: A finished commercial EDIT script, not a single generation prompt: a four-line technical/creative header (Render, Look, Grade, Audio+VO), then a shot list where each shot packs its timing, frame count, shot-size code and frame position into one bracket. Nine slots.
action-commercial.source_note: Reverse-engineered from a second community-supplied video prompt contributed by the user (a high-action car commercial). NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material, and a different shape from video-sequence above: that template's three locks exist to hold one PERSON steady across cuts, while this one is a vehicle/action piece with no character to lock, so it spends its header on capture technicals instead.

slots.label: Render
slots.does: The camera body and sensor, the film stock and grain, and a blanket physical-realism / anti-CGI negative - one compact technical header line.
slots.why: This template writes camera + grain + negative as ONE line rather than build_prompt.py's three separate layers, because that is how a real commercial brief is actually written. 'ARRI Alexa' is realism_lint's own camera-layer keyword and 'film grain' is its own grain-layer keyword, so even folded into one line this slot still reaches vocabulary the image side of the app already gates on.
slots.example: RENDER: Shot on ARRI Alexa 35, IMAX-grade sensor. 35mm film stock with natural film grain and organic imperfect textures throughout. Gravity-accurate physics. Raw tactile materials, no smooth surfaces, no artificial perfection, no CGI aesthetic.

slots.label: Look
slots.does: One line naming the cinematography genre, pacing and camera energy for the whole piece.
slots.why: Like video-sequence's own Style slot, this applies to every shot at once and is written once at the top rather than repeated per beat.
slots.example: LOOK: High-octane action cinematography, fast-paced commercial pacing, aggressive angles, dynamic kinetic energy.

slots.label: Grade
slots.does: The colour grade for the whole piece - the palette and the shadow treatment.
slots.why: Written once at the top exactly like the Look and Render lines, so every shot inherits the same grade instead of re-deciding it - the same continuity reasoning video-sequence's global Lighting line already uses.
slots.example: GRADE: Golden hour cinematic, rich contrasting sunset oranges and teals, deep crushed black shadows.

slots.label: Audio
slots.does: The scene's diegetic sound AND an explicit statement about music, together in one line.
slots.why: tools/sound_bank.json is effects-only and its linter rejects music vocabulary outright, which is why video-sequence above keeps Music and Sound as two separate slots. This template's source prompt states both in a single AUDIO line and opens by ruling music out explicitly - 'No music' is a real, working instruction, the same 'None is a real answer' reasoning the VO slot below and video-sequence's own Text slot already rely on.
slots.example: AUDIO: No music. Aggressive V8 engine revving, heavy bass rumble, mechanical click of paddle shifters, tire screeching, rushing wind transitioning at 00:10.0 into a massive supersonic whoosh, violent exhaust pops, fading engine echoes against a vast landscape, distant ocean waves.

slots.label: VO
slots.does: States whether there is a voice-over line at all - or explicitly that there is none.
slots.why: The same 'None is a real answer' rule as video-sequence's own on-screen-text slot: a video model volunteers a voice unprompted unless told not to, so writing 'VO: None' is a working instruction, not a blank line.
slots.example: VO: None

slots.label: Shot timing
slots.does: One shot's identity: the timestamp range, the frame count at the frame rate, the shot-size code (ECU/CU/MCU/MS/WS), and where in the frame it sits.
slots.why: A commercial edit is cut to the FRAME, not the second - the frame-count-at-fps figure is what an editor actually reads off this line, and the shot-size code is the same shorthand a director would write on a storyboard. video-shot's own six slots carry nothing this precise.
slots.example: S1 [00:00.0->00:02.0 | 48f @ 24fps | ECU | top center frame]

slots.label: Shot action
slots.does: What the subject and environment actually do in the shot - wardrobe, vehicle, motion - as one flowing paragraph.
slots.why: Written as prose, not a bracketed field, because this is the part of the shot a viewer actually sees; the technical bracket above and the camera line below sandwich it.
slots.example: Female driver's intense dark eyes glance sharply up into the carbon-fiber framed rearview mirror. Her space bun hair vibrates slightly from the intense engine rumble, eyelashes fluttering.

slots.label: Shot camera
slots.does: The camera's own behaviour for this shot - locked off or moving, the lens, the depth of field or shutter speed - placed at the END of the paragraph.
slots.why: The opposite order from video-shot's own camera-LEAD rule (motion_lint.py's rule one: start with the camera). That rule exists for a single shot fed straight to a Kling-style model; this template is a finished commercial edit script read by a person, where the action is what a viewer's eye follows and the camera note confirms it afterward. Use video-shot's own template, not this one, when writing a single generation prompt.
slots.example: Camera static, locked on the mirror, zero movement. Macro lens, shallow DOF blurring the road ahead.

slots.label: Cut
slots.does: Names the edit transition OUT of this shot.
slots.why: Every shot in the reference prompt ends with an explicit 'Cut: <type>' line - naming the edit is as load-bearing as naming the camera move, because an unstated cut defaults to a straight cut and the model has no way to know a smash cut or a whip pan was wanted.
slots.example: Cut: smash cut.

product-campaign.label: Product campaign portrait
product-campaign.summary: A banded commercial brief for one still: a talent portrait built around a product the subject is holding, written as twelve labelled slots rather than one flowing sentence. This is the image-side sibling of the High-action commercial template listed under video prompts - the same house style of a labelled brief, but a single frame with a person and a package in it instead of a timed shot list. Use it for a confectionery, drinks or beauty campaign frame where the pack has to stay legible and the talent has to carry an expression.
product-campaign.source_note: Reverse-engineered from a third community-supplied prompt contributed by the user - a confectionery campaign portrait. NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material. Two things in the source are deliberately NOT carried across, the same editorial call tools/macro_insert_bank.json already made about its own source: the '8K quality' claim, because tools/prompt_bank.json lists '8k' in `warn` as a phrase that does nothing on its own, and 'no text overlay, no watermark', which is already in prompt_bank's own `negatives` and rides every composed prompt for free. What IS carried across is the shape: a role line that sets the photographer's specialism before anything else, an identity band that states the anti-retouching constraint up front rather than in a trailing negative, and a dedicated PRODUCT band - the only template in this bank with one, and the reason it exists.

slots.label: Role
slots.does: One line casting the photographer: their specialism, and the register the whole frame is pitched in.
slots.why: A brief that opens by naming the kind of photographer who would shoot it constrains everything after it - lighting, styling and grade all follow from 'confectionery campaign' in a way they never follow from a list of adjectives. It is the cheapest line in the template and it does the most work.
slots.example: ROLE: A world-class commercial and lifestyle photographer specialising in bold, high-energy confectionery campaigns - vibrant colour storytelling with an editorial fashion influence.

slots.label: Identity
slots.does: Who the subject is - age, skin tone, hair, any accessory - and the preservation constraint that keeps them human.
slots.why: The preservation clause belongs HERE, at the top, not in a trailing negative. A model reads a brief in order, and 'authentic skin texture, no over-smoothing' stated alongside the subject is an instruction about how to render them; the same words appended at the end read as an afterthought it can trade away against 'polished commercial finish' further down.
slots.example: IDENTITY: A woman in her mid-twenties, warm medium skin tone, natural features. Long voluminous curly brown hair worn loose with real movement in it, held back from the face by a yellow-green tropical-print headband. Keep realistic anatomy, natural facial detail and authentic skin texture - no over-smoothing.

slots.label: Wardrobe
slots.does: The outfit, the skin it leaves visible, and any styling detail that carries colour - nails, jewellery, a manicure.
slots.why: In a campaign frame wardrobe is colour blocking, not clothing. The nails in the worked example are there because they repeat the pack's yellow into the foreground where the hand is; that is a styling decision doing compositional work, and it only happens if a slot exists to hold it.
slots.example: WARDROBE: A bold red strapless tube top, bare shoulders and collarbone visible in a clean editorial way. Bright yellow painted nails on both hands, picking up the pack's own colour. Playful and fashion-forward, strongly colour-coordinated.

slots.label: Composition
slots.does: Framing, camera height, lens, aspect ratio and where the focus falls - the whole optical setup as one band.
slots.why: Folded into one line rather than split across this app's separate composition, camera and lens layers, for the same reason action-commercial's Render slot folds camera and grain together: that is how a real commercial brief is written. The keywords here are this slot's own, so it stays honest about being a fold rather than pretending to be a gated layer.
slots.example: COMPOSITION: Medium close-up, chest-up framing, subject centred at a slight angle toward camera. Eye level. An 85mm portrait lens, aspect ratio 4:5, sharp on the face and the product with soft background falloff.

slots.label: Pose
slots.does: What both hands are doing, where the eyes go, and the one expression the frame is buying.
slots.why: Two hands, two jobs: one holds the product up, the other carries the performance. Briefing them separately is what stops the model inventing a limp second arm - and naming where the eyes look is what separates a caught-in-the-act expression from a posed one.
slots.example: POSE: Right hand raised near the mouth, a finger lightly touching the lips in a playful, mischievous gesture. Left hand raised at shoulder height holding the product toward camera. Dramatically playful and cheeky, eyes looking upward and to the side - caught in the act - mouth slightly open.

slots.label: Product
slots.does: The pack itself: what it is, the exact label text, the colours that text is set in, and how prominently it sits.
slots.why: The only slot of its kind in this bank, and the reason this template exists. Naming the label's exact words AND their colours is the single highest-value line in a product frame - a model told 'bold yellow lettering outlined in dark brown' renders legible type far more often than one told 'the logo is visible'. This is the same instruction tools/static_ad_bank.json carries as label_accuracy_phrase; state it here in full rather than relying on a trailing phrase.
slots.example: PRODUCT: The subject is holding a chocolate bar in its iconic orange wrapper. The logo faces camera and is clearly readable - bold yellow lettering outlined in dark brown. Packaging clean, undamaged and fully legible, positioned prominently as a second focal point beside the face.

slots.label: Lighting
slots.does: The light on the face and on the pack, and the separation between subject and background.
slots.why: A campaign frame lights two subjects, not one: a face that is beautifully lit above a pack that has fallen into shadow is a failed product shot. Say 'even across face and product' explicitly.
slots.example: LIGHTING: Bold, vibrant studio softbox lighting with strong fill and realistic shadows, even across both the face and the product. Warm highlights giving a soft bronzed glow on the skin, high contrast between subject and background.

slots.label: Background
slots.does: The backdrop as a designed gradient - named colours, and where each one sits top to bottom.
slots.why: 'Orange background' produces a flat wall. Naming the gradient by position - deep at the bottom, glowing at the top - produces depth behind the subject and is what makes a seamless read as a lit studio rather than as a fill layer.
slots.example: BACKGROUND: A seamless studio backdrop in a rich burnt-orange gradient - deep amber-brown at the bottom, warm terracotta through the middle, glowing orange at the top. Smooth and immersive.

slots.label: Skin and texture
slots.does: The surface detail that has to survive the polish - skin, hair strands, fabric weave.
slots.why: This band and the OUTPUT band pull in opposite directions on purpose: one asks for a clean commercial finish, the other refuses to buy it with skin. Writing both down is what keeps the tension explicit instead of letting the model resolve it toward plastic.
slots.example: SKIN AND TEXTURE: Natural skin texture with visible pores and a subtle glow, high detail in individual hair strands and in the fabric grain of the top. A clean commercial finish that is not airbrushed.

slots.label: Colour and mood
slots.does: The palette as a named set of colours, plus the feeling the frame is pitched at.
slots.why: Naming the palette as a list - red, orange, yellow - rather than as a mood word is what keeps the wardrobe, the pack and the backdrop in one colour story instead of three.
slots.example: COLOUR AND MOOD: A bold saturated palette of red, orange and yellow with tropical accents, high contrast and realistic colour balance. Playful, energetic and youthful - editorial fashion meeting confectionery advertising.

slots.label: Output
slots.does: The capture body the whole frame is pretending to be, stated once at the end.
slots.why: The source asked for '8K quality' and that is dropped here on purpose - prompt_bank.json lists '8k' in warn because a resolution claim does nothing that a real camera name does not do better. Naming a body that is actually full-frame and mirrorless earns the CAMERA layer honestly, which a number never does. The three core triggers and 'sharp focus' are what carry the core and grain layers, and they are why this template's worked example clears the full 8/8 gate rather than merely describing a frame - tests/test_anatomy.py pins that, because an example a reader is meant to paste should not be one the app would refuse.
slots.example: OUTPUT: Shot on a Canon EOS R5, full-frame mirrorless - photorealistic, ultra-realistic, true-to-life textures, sharp focus throughout.

slots.label: Framing
slots.does: The one thing that must not be cropped, stated as a requirement rather than a preference.
slots.why: A separate final line, not folded into COMPOSITION, because it is a different kind of instruction: composition says where to put things, this says what the frame is not allowed to lose. In a product frame the pack is what gets clipped, and it is the only element whose loss makes the image worthless.
slots.example: FRAMING: Subject and product must both be fully visible within the frame, with clear focus on the facial expression and the product placement - no cropping of key elements.

candid-editorial.label: Candid editorial close-up
candid-editorial.summary: A close portrait that has to read as a photograph someone took, not one someone made: found light, a real place behind, and an exact crop. Thirteen slots. Where the beauty macro listed above spends its slots on skin at magnification in a controlled studio, this one spends them on the two things a studio removes - the light you did not set, and the room you did not build - and then asks for the same skin detail anyway.
candid-editorial.source_note: Reverse-engineered from a fourth community-supplied prompt contributed by the user - a golden-hour cafe profile portrait. NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material. It is deliberately NOT a second beauty-macro: that template is a studio macro (tools/macro_insert_bank.json pairs it with a Hasselblad, a 100mm macro lens and beauty-box lighting), while this one is explicitly anti-studio - its source says 'no artificial lighting, no studio look - this must feel like a real candid photo taken on a phone or mirrorless camera in a cafe'. The two answer different questions, so they are two templates rather than one with a switch. Dropped from the source, the same editorial call macro_insert_bank.json and product-campaign already made: the '8K, ultra-high resolution' claim, because prompt_bank.json lists '8k' in `warn` - a resolution number does nothing a named body and a named aperture do not do better. Also trimmed: most of the source's fourteen-item negative list, because 'no cartoon, no CGI, no plastic skin' are already prompt_bank.json's own `negatives` and ride every composed prompt for free. What survives in the negatives slot is only what that list does NOT already cover.

slots.label: Frame
slots.does: The shot in one breath: how close, what angle, and the fact that it is candid rather than posed.
slots.why: Leading with 'candid, unposed' sets the register for every slot after it. A prompt that establishes this first gets a subject who happens to be there; one that mentions it last gets a posed portrait with the word 'candid' attached.
slots.example: an ultra-realistic, true-to-life, lifelike close-up three-quarter profile portrait of a young woman at an outdoor cafe, candid and unposed

slots.label: Crop
slots.does: Exactly where the frame cuts - which features are in, and which are deliberately out.
slots.why: The single most-skipped decision in a close portrait, and the one that decides whether it reads as editorial or as a passport photo. Naming both edges ('above the forehead', 'below the lips') is what stops the model defaulting to a centred head with air all round it.
slots.example: her face filling most of the frame, cropped just above the forehead and below the lips for an intimate editorial crop

slots.label: Gaze
slots.does: Where the eyes go, and the thought behind them.
slots.why: Off-camera is what makes a candid candid. An eyeline into the lens is a portrait of someone being photographed; an eyeline past it is a portrait of someone thinking.
slots.example: her gaze looking slightly forward and off-camera, thoughtful and unaware of the lens

slots.label: Skin
slots.does: The skin at close range - pores, tonal variation, the shine the light actually makes.
slots.why: This is the slot the whole template is protecting. At this crop, skin is most of the picture, and an oil sheen on the forehead and cheekbones is the difference between a face and a mask. State the sheen positively: it is a thing the light is doing, not a flaw to permit.
slots.example: visible skin pores, faint freckles and slight redness across the cheeks and nose, a realistic oil sheen on the forehead and cheekbones catching the sun, slight imperfections preserved rather than retouched away

slots.label: Features
slots.does: Eyes, lashes, brows and lips at the level of individual hairs and real moisture.
slots.why: Separate from the skin slot because they fail differently: skin fails by being too smooth, features fail by being too uniform. A brow drawn as a shape reads as makeup; a brow drawn as irregular individual hairs reads as a brow.
slots.example: eyes sharp and glossy with light reflecting naturally inside the pupils, fine individual eyelashes, natural brows with visible hair strands, lips soft and slightly parted with realistic moisture

slots.label: Hair
slots.does: How it is worn, and the strands that escape - flyaways and baby hairs along the hairline.
slots.why: Pulled-back hair is a trap: a model given only 'tied back' renders a helmet. The flyaways are what make it hair, and they are only ever there if you ask.
slots.example: hair pulled back tightly to reveal the forehead and temples, tiny flyaway and baby hairs visible along the hairline, individual strands crisp and naturally lit

slots.label: Light
slots.does: Light that was already there - its direction, its hour, and the exact features it lands on.
slots.why: The anti-studio slot. Naming which side it comes from AND which planes it touches - forehead, cheekbone, nose bridge, upper lip - is what produces directional light instead of an even wash. A studio setup named here would undo the whole template.
slots.example: warm directional golden-hour sunlight from the left, soft natural daylight with realistic shadows, catching the forehead, cheekbone, nose bridge and upper lip with a gentle falloff on the far side of the face

slots.label: Background
slots.does: The real place behind her, and how far out of focus it goes.
slots.why: A studio removes the room; this template needs it. The instruction that matters is the tension - alive but not competing - because a background described only as 'blurred' comes back empty, and one described only as 'a cafe' comes back sharp and distracting.
slots.example: a European outdoor cafe behind her - wooden tables, wicker chairs, glassware - softly blurred, alive but not distracting, warm sunlight filtering through

slots.label: Camera
slots.does: The body, the focal length and the aperture that produce this depth of field.
slots.why: The bokeh in the slot above is a CONSEQUENCE of this one, not an independent wish. Naming a wide aperture on a long-ish prime is what earns the creamy background; asking for 'creamy bokeh' without it asks for an effect with no cause.
slots.example: shot on a full-frame mirrorless camera with an 85mm lens at f/1.8, shallow depth of field, natural bokeh, the face tack-sharp while the cafe melts behind her

slots.label: Grade
slots.does: The colour treatment, and the processing this photograph has NOT had.
slots.why: The refusals carry the slot: no HDR and no oversharpening name the two artefacts that most reliably give away a generated image, and they are not in prompt_bank's standing negatives.
slots.example: natural color grading, warm golden highlights and realistic contrast, no HDR look and no oversharpening

slots.label: Mood
slots.does: The feeling in three or four words, and the world it belongs to.
slots.why: Last of the positive slots because it is the least specific. It arbitrates the close calls the slots above left open - how parted the lips, how soft the falloff - and it can only do that once they are all on the table.
slots.example: effortless, modern and intimate - a behind-the-scenes moment from a lifestyle shoot

slots.label: Capture
slots.does: The one line that says this is a photograph: sharpness, and any grain the sensor actually put there.
slots.why: Separate from the camera slot because it is about the FILE rather than the glass. It is also where the source's '8K' claim was dropped: a resolution number is not a capture property, and prompt_bank.json lists '8k' in warn precisely because it does nothing on its own.
slots.example: sharp focus on the near eye, real photographic detail, subtle sensor noise in the shadows

slots.label: Negatives
slots.does: Only the refusals that prompt_bank.json's own standing negatives do NOT already cover.
slots.why: The source listed fourteen, and most of them - no cartoon, no CGI, no plastic skin - are already appended to every prompt this app composes. Repeating them costs words and teaches nothing. What is left is specific to this shot: the studio look it must not fall back into, and the lighting cliches that would undo the found-light slot.
slots.example: no studio backdrop, no glamour lighting, no artificial glow, no fake bokeh, no beauty filter
